questions.q: What is the key difference between invoice validation and invoice approval?
options: They are the same process with two different names
Validation checks whether the invoice is internally clean; approval is a separate workflow deciding whether a human signs off on paying it
Approval happens before validation
Approval only applies to credit memos
questions.explain: Validation and approval are two independent status fields, run by two different systems: validation logic versus a BPM/human workflow engine.

questions.q: What technology underlies Oracle Fusion's invoice approval rules?
options: The same validation engine used for matching tolerances
A dedicated Payables-only approval database
Approval Management extensions (AMX) of Oracle SOA Suite and Oracle Human Workflow
The supplier portal
questions.explain: Invoice approval rules are built using AMX, the shared human workflow technology also used for other business documents.

questions.q: Why might an invoice have an approval status of 'Not Required'?
options: Because all invoices always skip approval
Because the invoice failed validation
Because the supplier is Prospective
Because the organization has configured certain invoices, like those fully matched to an approved PO, to not require a separate approval workflow
questions.explain: Whether approval is required at all is a configuration decision; fully PO-matched invoices are a common case for skipping it.

questions.q: What is the difference between sequential and parallel approval routing?
options: Sequential asks approvers one after another; parallel asks multiple approvers at the same time
Sequential is only used for credit memos
Parallel routing means no one needs to approve
There is no functional difference
questions.explain: Sequential routing requires one approver to act before moving to the next; parallel routing asks multiple approvers simultaneously.

questions.q: What happens when an invoice is Rejected during approval?
options: It is automatically paid anyway
It is automatically merged with another invoice
It is a distinct, actionable outcome signaling the invoice typically needs correction and resubmission
Nothing changes; it remains in the same pending state
questions.explain: Rejection is a clear, distinct status meaning someone with authority declined the invoice, usually requiring correction and resubmission.
